perspective: Adversarial verification of Daisy Finance chartfield, account, funding, costing, monitoring, and access workflow against all three interview transcripts and all three derived Markdown artifacts.

findings.claim: The Finance handoff is an appointment already processed by HR/Laura, with salary and chartfield data in the shared appointment worksheet; Finance then acts on verified appointments.
evidence: Call with Laura Hemphill (1).docx:123-130 — Laura says she verifies Oracle and Daisy's team filters for verified records to do costing.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:1028-1049 — Daisy describes Finance checking the chartfield, then recording status/date/initials in the worksheet.
daisy_finance_stage.md:15-18, 67-68 — derived handoff model.
student_hiring_pipeline.md:27-31, 89-94, 109-114 — Laura verification precedes Daisy costing.
findings.risk: The worksheet is acting as the operational handoff, but no authoritative record/version or handoff acknowledgement is established.
findings.recommendation: Treat the worksheet handoff as observed current behavior only; require an explicit record identity, revision/history, and handoff timestamp before automation.

findings.claim: Finance verifies the chartfield and checks/obtains confirmation from the faculty member or PI before costing.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:1028-1049 — Finance enters/checks the chartfield, verifies it with the faculty member, and changes the row status after entry.
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:79-86 — Mayra says faculty confirmation is required because funding may change and protects against a defaulted account.
daisy_finance_stage.md:17-22, 101-106 — derived workflow says verify with faculty/PI and flags whether confirmation is always required.
findings.risk: The transcripts do not establish whether Finance reconfirms every chartfield or only confirms when something is missing, changed, or suspect; 'faculty/PI' is also not defined as an authority rule.
findings.recommendation: Do not encode universal auto-confirmation. Record confirmation actor, date, source, and scope; leave the always-versus-exception policy open.

findings.claim: Missing or unfunded chartfields loop back through faculty contact, worksheet update, and re-verification.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:42-44 — Daisy describes requesting an account when the chartfield was not provided.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:1028-1049 — Finance verifies the chartfield; if there is no money, the team discusses it with the faculty member and changes the chartfield.
daisy_finance_stage.md:19-22, 37-44, 85-89 — missing and no-money branches return through worksheet update to verification.
mayra_student_hiring_flow.md:79-80, 85-90 — defaulted-account handling refers back to the faculty confirmation record.
findings.risk: The evidence does not define a terminal state for no response, no valid account, or repeated failed funding checks.
findings.recommendation: Add bounded exception states and escalation/stop rules; retain each rejected or superseded funding value rather than overwriting it.

findings.claim: Finance maintains an account list organized by departmental accounts, active grants, startup accounts, and accountable officer/PI; Box is the working file and FAST is a related source/query plane.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:214-257 — Daisy describes the college account list, active grants, departmental/auxiliary accounts, PI-associated chartfields, and frequent cleanup/updates.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:263-279 — department accounts/active grants are accounts; Research Foundation and foundation pages are funds and may have convenience chartfields.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:294-311 — Daisy says the information is in FAST but may require Matt/Eric; until then a manually updated spreadsheet is usable.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:343-355 — the reconciliation/account files are stored in Box under Daisy's folder.
daisy_finance_stage.md:11-13, 56-80 — derived account/source model.
findings.risk: Box, the local spreadsheet, and FAST are not assigned explicit authority, synchronization direction, freshness guarantees, or conflict resolution.
findings.recommendation: Declare one system of record for account validity/funding and label Box/worksheet/FAST as source, mirror, or working projection with refresh and conflict rules.

findings.claim: Multi-account costing requires a per-pay-period distribution whose percentages total 100%; fringe and pay-period calendars are lookup/configuration inputs that change over time.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:87-101, 167-189 — distributions are calculated per biweekly pay period, entered in Oracle, and must account for multiple accounts.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:376-397 — Daisy describes the distribution formula and the requirement to calculate it manually/consistently.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:413-450 — fringe rates are lookup-driven and change by category/year.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:454-472 — pay periods/check dates are maintained annually and costing must be changed in Oracle by the relevant deadline.
daisy_finance_stage.md:23-26, 73-76 — derived distribution and Oracle steps.
findings.risk: The evidence proves the calculation inputs exist but not validation behavior, rounding/tolerance, effective-date handling, or whether all appointment classes use the same fringe/distribution rules.
findings.recommendation: Require effective-dated rate/calendar tables, deterministic total validation, rounding policy, and class-specific rule confirmation before implementation.

findings.claim: Finance enters costing in Oracle and monitors active appointments, including stale/ended appointments and termination.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:472-482 — RSA checks and Oracle costing deadlines matter.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:892-931 — Daisy manually summarizes active appointments across action tabs, questions stale records with Mayra/Laura/faculty, and wants an active-appointment summary.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:1021-1049 — Finance marks worksheet status/date/initials and monitors active appointments.
daisy_finance_stage.md:26-31, 49-53, 77-80 — derived Oracle, monitoring, stale/ended, and termination flow.
findings.risk: The exact Oracle deadline, monitoring cadence, termination authority, and meaning of the post-green status are unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Do not infer 'page' as 'paid' or any other terminal status; capture exact statuses, deadline owner, cadence, and termination transition from Finance.

findings.claim: Finance reconciliation data is sensitive and access is intended to be role-limited, while some cross-team visibility is useful.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:516-524 — Daisy says Finance has access to sensitive reconciliation data while Mayra and Laura do not; a dedicated Box folder and explicit access list are acceptable.
Call with Daisy Matos.docx:529-539 — Ian proposes that everybody can see anything while only selected users can edit.
Call with Mayra Morfin (1).docx:209-226, 340-352 — Mayra asks for restricted creation/edit access and says she should view Laura's screen but not edit HR statuses because she lacks Oracle access.
daisy_finance_stage.md:11-13 — derived artifact preserves the sensitive Finance boundary.
findings.risk: A broad read-all model conflicts with the stated sensitivity and least-privilege boundary. No field-level visibility, role matrix, or access audit behavior is established.
findings.recommendation: Block security-sensitive implementation until roles, field/record scopes, edit authorities, Box sharing, and audit logging are explicitly defined; default to least privilege, not universal visibility.

findings.claim: The current process has an audit marker (status plus date/initials), but it is not yet a complete audit trail.
evidence: Call with Daisy Matos.docx:1035-1049 — row status is changed and date/initials are recorded after Finance entry.
Call with Laura Hemphill (1).docx:697-708, 1045-1058 — overwriting spreadsheet rows loses prior requests and audit evidence.
student_hiring_pipeline.md:56-60 — derived artifact identifies the missing audit trail.
findings.risk: Status/date/initials do not preserve prior chartfields, funding decisions, rejected values, confirmations, or Oracle reconciliation evidence.
findings.recommendation: Preserve append-only change events or equivalent history for chartfield, funding, distribution, confirmation, Oracle entry, and termination actions.

missing_or_ambiguous: Exact Finance row statuses after the green in-progress state; transcript rendering says 'page' and the derived artifact says probably 'paid' (daisy_finance_stage.md:27, 101-106).
Whether faculty/PI confirmation is mandatory for every record or only for changed, missing, or suspect chartfields (daisy_finance_stage.md:104-106).
Which source is authoritative among FAST, Box account spreadsheets, appointment worksheet, Oracle, and any Power BI projection; no sync/freshness/conflict policy is stated.
Exact Oracle costing deadlines, responsible Finance role, and monitoring cadence (daisy_finance_stage.md:102-104).
Whether graduate-student appointments receive fringe or multi-account distributions, versus the faculty/staff examples Daisy demonstrated (daisy_finance_stage.md:104-106).
Termination authority and exact state transition when an appointment is stale, superseded, or ended.
No-response and no-valid-account escalation/terminal behavior in the missing/unfunded loops.
Role/field-level access matrix, including whether Finance users may see HR data and whether HR users may see any Finance reconciliation details; current proposal conflicts with stated sensitivity.
Whether the Finance workflow is a single shared system or a projection over Box/FAST/Oracle; Daisy explicitly leaves that architecture unresolved (Call with Daisy Matos.docx:1091-1109).
